blocks.text: Mastering Slack navigation on your Mac

As an HR generalist, your day involves constant switching between channels. You move from payroll discussions to performance review threads. The fastest way to move is the Quick Switcher. Press Command + K to open it. Type the name of the channel or person you need. Press Enter to jump there immediately.

If you lose your place, use the sidebar effectively. Keep your most active channels at the top. Right-click a channel name to move it to your starred list. This keeps high-priority employee queries visible at all times.
Use keyboard shortcuts for faster communication

items: Command + /: Open the full list of Slack shortcuts.
Shift + Enter: Create a line break in your message instead of sending it.
Command + B: Bold text to highlight critical HR policy updates.
Command + I: Italicize text for emphasis during sensitive conversations.
Command + ,: Open your Slack preferences to manage notification schedules.

blocks.text: Manage HR interruptions with Slack status

HR work requires deep focus for documentation and reporting. Constant notifications break your concentration. Use the status feature to signal your availability. Click your profile photo in the bottom left. Select Update status. Set a clear label like Drafting Contracts or In a Meeting. This reduces the number of incoming pings.
Use /dnd followed by a time to pause all notifications. For example, /dnd 60 minutes gives you an hour of uninterrupted time to finish your HR reports.

Handling sensitive HR data in Slack

Security is mandatory for HR. Never share sensitive employee data in public channels. Use private channels or direct messages for confidential discussions. If you need to share a document, use the secure file upload feature. Check if your company has a data retention policy for Slack messages.

Sometimes Slack slows down or stops updating. This happens after long periods of use. The best fix is to clear the cache. Go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This forces the app to refresh its local data. It often resolves missing notifications or stuck threads.

Employees ask the same questions repeatedly. Use the Saved Items feature to keep snippets of common answers. When you get a question about holiday leave, search your saved items. Copy the text and paste it into the chat. You can also use Lazur to dictate these responses quickly.

Main channel feeds get cluttered fast. Always reply in a thread for specific employee issues. Hover over the message. Click the speech bubble icon to start a thread. This keeps the main channel clean for general announcements. It also makes it easier to track the history of a specific conversation.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Slack for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate Slack for you. It points at buttons or guides you through the steps so you can perform the action yourself.

faq.question: Does Slack require a specific macOS version?
faq.answer: Yes. Slack requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer for the latest supported versions as of November 2026.

faq.question: How do I find a specific message in a long conversation?
faq.answer: Press Command + F while inside the conversation to search only that channel. You can also use modifiers like from: or has: to narrow down your search results.

faq.question: Is my data private when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur only sees your screen and listens to your voice while you hold the shortcut. No data is stored or used to train AI models.
